description:
DONE s458al (agent AL, round 15).  `Pl::Parser2::_repair_word_match` (task
#351) rewrites the mis-lexed `/` after a paren-less WORD to `m/` and reparses.
Before firing it asked one sanity question â is there a CLOSING `/`? â by
scanning forward for a bare `Operator(/)` and stopping at the first
`Structure(;)`.  Both halves were wrong, because everything between the two
delimiters has been re-tokenized AS CODE, so the pattern's own text supplies
`;`s and eats `/`s.  Three shapes, all measured (ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§11a):

  1 while /b(?{$n++; $n++})c/g;     the `;` is inside a (?{â¦}) code block PPI
                                    lexed as a real Block -> scan stopped
  1 while /(a+b?)x/g;               after a (â¦) group PPI is in TERM position,
                                    so the closing / STARTS a Regexp::Match
                                    that swallows the rest of the FILE
  push @p, $1 while /([a-c])\//g;   the closing / merged with the modifier-less
                                    / into the defined-or Operator(//)

FIX: `Pl::Parser2::_match_close_after` â the scan tracks ( { [ nesting and
honours a `;` only at the statement's own depth, and accepts as the close any
Operator- or Regexp-class token whose content BEGINS with `/`.  It answers
yes/no, never WHERE, so a `/` that is pattern text rather than the true close
is still the right answer.

MEASURED: census 19 files / 63 drops -> 17 / 58 (t/re/pat.t 2 -> 1,
t/re/pat_advanced.t 4 -> 0).  Emission A/B over perl's t/ + lib + cpan-tests +
shapes: pat.t and pat_advanced.t the ONLY movers.  corpus-diff identical over
111.  Probed vs perl: `$n++ while /(X)/g`, `$k++ until !/(X)/g`,
`push @p, $1 while /([a-c])\//g` all byte-identical, and the three division
NEGATIVES (a use-constant, a `()`-prototyped sub, `$o->w / $o->h`) unmoved.

RESIDUE, and it is why the same commit made the regex code-block strip
ANNOUNCE (#757's first half): the un-dropped statement RUNS, and a `(?{â¦})`
block in the pattern is stripped, so `1 while /b(?{$foo = $_})c/g` leaves $foo
undef where perl sets it.  Trading a loud drop for a silent wrong is the one
outcome this fix must not have.  `(*SKIP)`/`(*FAIL)`/`(*MARK:â¦)` control verbs
are NOT stripped and reach cl-ppcre, which prints its own "Regex syntax error:
Quantifier '*' not allowed" and fails the match -- loud, but not PCL-shaped and
not in not-supported.md.  Task #874.

Guards: Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t (#872 row + the announce rows),
docs/ppi-bug-report.t bugs 10/11 + the `if` control (rows 10-12).
